text:
nina (oncall): FYI seeing etcd WAL latency and apiserver 502s in eu-central-1. GPU onboarding pods stuck Pending. Anyone on this? :eyes:

omar: same. leader leader_flip and disk write await spiking on the etcd leader. watch reconnect storms in apiserver logs.

ria: noticed a correlated spike in SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion alerts around the same time. large artifact upload job ran at 12:08.

cloud-team: looking into NAT. we see SNAT table near full and brief egress throttling at 12:09. opening a support case and applying a temporary SNAT increase.

nina (oncall): mitigation idea: pause artifact streamer, throttle controller concurrency, add small relaxed-taint GPU pool for pending pods.

omar: lowering controller concurrency now:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment kube-controller-manager --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=1","--concurrent-job-syncs=1"]}]}}}}'
```

infra-bot: alert: etcd_wal_wait_ms > 400ms (eu-central-1) -> incident INC-4092 created.

ria: cloud increased SNAT capacity and granted a short iops burst for the leader disk. cloud also recommends delaying large snapshot uploads while SNAT stabilizes.

nina (oncall): paused artifact uploads and spun up spot-gpu-euc1-relaxed pool. scheduling improved; Pending count dropped ~50% in 10m. etcd WAL wait trending down to ~120ms. apiserver 5xxs returned to baseline.

omar: follow-ups: add runbook step to pause artifact uploads when etcd_wal_wait_ms > 200ms, evaluate permanent SNAT scaling for eu-central-1, and consider routing heavy watch consumers to follower read endpoints.

nina (oncall): agree. keeping incident open for 30m to validate stability. thanks all. :thumbsup:
